A adds explicitly prohibited public association APIs and multipart machinery, then bypasses FilesService.Add.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature and correctly uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", preserving filename and content.","B’s upload body is replayable and its retry test exercises streamed content from an *os.File across a 429.","B centralizes request options, request execution, decoding, and response validation in one helper, whereas A duplicates the body of Add inside Upload.","A explicitly violates the contract by adding six association options, changing FilesOption internals, and introducing NewFileWithFields instead of reusing NewFile directly without extension of scope."],"risks_a":["Upload does not route through FilesService.Add; it duplicates request construction, response decoding, and error handling.","Adds association fields and public WithFile*ID options despite the explicit prohibition.","Changes the established multipart helper and adds unrelated field support solely for the prohibited associations."],"risks_b":["Changes Add behavior by eagerly buffering every caller-supplied body, contrary to preserving its existing lower-level behavior and potentially increasing memory use.","Upload calls a new private add helper rather than routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","Validation combines two distinct cases into one error, and tests omit the required validation and source-reader failure coverage."]}
